 Revised: Oct 24, 2016           Rosetta Spacecraft                        -226
                       http://www.esa.int/export/SPECIALS/Rosetta/

 NOTE: To generate an ephemeris of Rosetta with respect to comet 67P, set the 
       coordinate center to "@1000012". Such relative data is available only 
       over 2014-Mar-3 to 2016-Oct-05, currently based on a merge of mission
       comet solutions CORB_DV_117_02_00186, CORB_DV_180_01_00255, and 
       CORB_DV_257_02___T19_00344.

       Due to the spacecraft's close proximity to the comet and the comet's 
       irregular shape, some quantities such as sub-solar/center latitude and 
       longitude (cartographic coordinates) may not be meaningful.
 
 BACKGROUND:
  After entering orbit around Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 2014-Aug-6 
  at 09:06 UTC, Rosetta released a small lander (Philae) onto the icy nucleus
  on November 12 @ 13:04 UTC, with landing four hours later. It then spent the 
  next two years and 55 days orbiting the comet as it move closer in toward 
  the Sun. 

  On 2016-September-30 @ 10:39:28 UTC, the Rosetta spacecraft ended its mission
  by landing on the comet in the Ma'at region.

  On the way to the comet, Rosetta received gravity assists from Earth and 
  Mars, and encountered main belt asteroids 2867 Steins and 21 Lutetia.

 ROSETTA SPACECRAFT:
  Launch (Ariane-5G)= Mar 2, 2004 07:17:51 UTC
  Size (orbiter)    = 2.8 x 2.1 x 2.0 meters, two 14m solar panels (64 m^2)
  Communications    = 2.2 m diameter dish (steerable high-gain)
  Mass              = 3000 kg (fully fuelled; 1670 kg propellant) 
                        165 kg of science payload for the orbiter 
                        100 kg of science payload for the lander 

  Flybys:       
   Earth: 2005-Mar-04 22:10 UTC (8340 km from center, ~1962 km altitude)
   Mars : 2007-Feb-25           (250 km altitude)
   Earth: 2007-Nov-13 20:57 UTC (11,678 km (center), alt=0.83 Earth-radii)
   2867 Steins: 2008-Sep-05 18:37 UTC (800 km, 8.6 km/s)
   Earth: 2009-Nov-13 07:45:40 UTC (alt~2490 km, lat=-8.2 deg, long.=109.0 deg)
   21 Lutetia: 2010-Jul-10 15:44:45 UTC (event time, 3235 km, 15 km/s)

*******************************************************************************
 
TIME

  Barycentric Dynamical Time ("TDB" or T_eph) output was requested. This
continuous coordinate time is equivalent to the relativistic proper time
of a clock at rest in a reference frame co-moving with the solar system
barycenter but outside the system's gravity well. It is the independent
variable in the solar system relativistic equations of motion.

  TDB runs at a uniform rate of one SI second per second and is independent
of irregularities in Earth's rotation.
 
CALENDAR SYSTEM

  Mixed calendar mode was active such that calendar dates after AD 1582-Oct-15
(if any) are in the modern Gregorian system. Dates prior to 1582-Oct-5 (if any)
are in the Julian calendar system, which is automatically extended for dates
prior to its adoption on 45-Jan-1 BC.  The Julian calendar is useful for
matching historical dates. The Gregorian calendar more accurately corresponds
to the Earth's orbital motion and seasons. A "Gregorian-only" calendar mode is
available if such physical events are the primary interest.

REFERENCE FRAME AND COORDINATES

  International Celestial Reference Frame (ICRF)

    The ICRF is an adopted reference frame whose axes are defined relative to 
    fixed extragalactic radio sources distributed across the sky.

    The ICRF was aligned with the prior FK5/J2000 dynamical system at the ~0.02 
    arcsecond level but is not identical and has no associated standard epoch.

  Symbol meaning [1 au= 149597870.700 km, 1 day= 86400.0 s]:

    JDTDB    Julian Day Number, Barycentric Dynamical Time
      X      X-component of position vector (au)
      Y      Y-component of position vector (au)
      Z      Z-component of position vector (au)

ABERRATIONS AND CORRECTIONS

 Geometric state vectors have NO corrections or aberrations applied.
